To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
common knowledge is the key to understanding the dynamics of decision making and information acquisition in a social setting.
common knowledge is the basis of common decisions, and that a dialogue in decisions leads to common decisions.

(a) the common knowledge of a rational decision by each agent implies a common decision for all agents; (b) a “dialogue”, or “conversation”, in which the agents make rational decisions based on their common knowledge of each other's decisions, leads to a common rational decision; and (c) if agents have common knowledge of each others' beliefs, then they cannot trade with each other.
